# DriftSense Pilot — Devpost submission

## Elevator pitch

On a periodic semiconductor array every copy of a structure looks the same, so a
template matcher can confidently send the microscope to the wrong copy.
DriftSense Pilot reads each edge's unique roughness with an OpenCV 5 pipeline,
says how sure it is, and lets an agent re-image or hand the decision to a human
instead of guessing.

## The problem

Scanning electron microscopes navigate to a measurement site by matching a
reference patch against a search image. On FinFET fins, DRAM-like contact arrays
and line gratings the patch matches a whole lattice of near-identical replicas.
A confident commit to the wrong replica is not a ranking error: the stage moves
to the wrong cell and every downstream measurement inherits the offset. Asking
for another image is cheap by comparison.

## What it does

- **Localises** a reference patch in a periodic search image with a ten-stage
  OpenCV pipeline (S0–S9) that scores candidates on their line-edge-roughness
  residual, at lattice-consistent offsets only, and returns ranked candidates, a
  calibrated margin, a commit-or-escalate decision and explainability images.
- **Acts** through an active-perception agent that drives a virtual SEM: it
  raises dwell, widens the field of view or re-localises when the evidence is
  weak, commits a stage move only when the margin clears a calibrated threshold,
  and otherwise escalates with an approval card for a human.
- **Runs** as a web app on AWS: a static UI, an HTTP API on arm64 Lambda, and a
  Graviton worker built from the COOL 3.1 AMI, plus an MCP server that exposes
  the same guarded tools to any MCP client.

## How we built it

### OpenCV 5 usage

★ marks KleidiCV-listed operations that COOL can accelerate on Graviton. The
full call list per module is in [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

| Stage | Purpose | OpenCV calls |
|---|---|---|
| S0 Ingest / QC | Decode, grayscale, mean/std, saturation, SNR proxy | `imdecode`, `cvtColor` ★, `meanStdDev`, `minMaxLoc` ★ |
| S1 Lattice | Lattice vectors, period and angle in the Fourier domain | `getOptimalDFTSize`, `createHanningWindow`, `dft`, `magnitude`, `log` |
| S2 Rectify | De-rotation hypotheses on a coarse copy | `pyrDown` ★, `getRotationMatrix2D`, `warpPerspective` ★ |
| S3 Roughness residual | Remove the ideal periodic pattern, keep edge roughness | `sepFilter2D` ★, `GaussianBlur` ★, `Sobel` ★, `erode` ★, `dilate` ★, `magnitude` |
| S4 Candidate scoring | Residual matching at lattice-consistent offsets | `matchTemplate` (`TM_CCOEFF_NORMED`), `dilate` ★ NMS, `minMaxLoc` ★ |
| S5 DRAM contour | Planned contact-array fingerprint | scaffold in this build, not on the path |
| S6 Cascade | Re-rank a close short-list with the frozen v1 fingerprint | NumPy |
| S7 Confidence | Robust z-margin and isotonic calibration | NumPy |
| S8 Subpixel | Final sub-pixel offset | `phaseCorrelate`, `findTransformECC` |
| S9 Explain | Heatmaps, candidate gallery, overlay | `applyColorMap`, `addWeighted`, `drawMarker`, `putText`, `imencode` |

The stack pins `opencv-python-headless` 5.0.0.93 for development and the
COOL 3.1 build on the worker.

### AWS and COOL

CloudFront and a private S3 bucket serve the UI. An API Gateway HTTP API
invokes a FastAPI app on arm64 Lambda (via Mangum) that presigns uploads,
records jobs in DynamoDB and enqueues them on SQS with a dead-letter queue. An
Auto Scaling group of c8g.large Graviton workers built from the COOL 3.1 AMI
runs the v2 engine, the agent and the virtual SEM, importing OpenCV from the
COOL environment only. Results go to encrypted S3 with a short lifecycle;
per-stage metrics, a dashboard, a canary and alarms live in CloudWatch, with an
AWS Budgets alert on cost. GitHub Actions deploys the CDK app through OIDC. See
[docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

**COOL benchmark: campaign pending.** The COOL campaign (x86 with PyPI
OpenCV, Graviton with PyPI OpenCV, Graviton with COOL) has not run yet, so this
submission makes no COOL speed-up or cost claim. The method and the
reproduction steps are in [docs/COOL_EVIDENCE.md](docs/COOL_EVIDENCE.md), which
is regenerated from the benchmark results file once it exists.

### Agent loop and MCP

A deterministic, auditable rules policy reads the margin, SNR, lattice
uncertainty and the remaining step and dose budget after every localisation and
picks the next tool: more dwell, a wider field of view, more rectification
hypotheses, a refinement pass, a commit, or a human-approval request. The
runner, not the policy, enforces the safety gates: it refuses any commit below
the calibrated threshold, caps the number of steps, applies a dose budget and a
per-tool timeout, and logs every step as a JSONL trace whose commit event
records the margin and threshold that justified it. An optional LLM planner may
only propose perception tools. The same six pydantic-validated tools are served
over MCP with FastMCP (`python -m driftsense.agent.mcp_server`).

**What the sealed numbers say, including where v2 loses:**

- **v2 single-shot top-1 is below both baselines.** Its pooled top-1 is

  52.5% [SEALED]<!--src:results/sealed/ncc.json#top1.pooled fmt=pct--> for NCC; the intervals overlap with v1's.
  v2 is not a better single-shot point estimator.
- **The right answer is almost always in the candidate set**: v2 set-recall on
  structured pairs is 96.7% (95% CI 91.7–98.7%) [SEALED]<!--src:results/sealed/v2_single.json#set_recall.pooled_structured fmt=pct ci-->.
  What is hard is telling the true copy from its replicas.
- **v2 abstains on every sealed pair.** At the calibrated threshold it committed
  on 0 [SEALED]<!--src:results/sealed/v2_single.json#commits.n fmt=int--> pairs, so its false-confident rate of
  0.0% [SEALED]<!--src:results/sealed/v2_single.json#false_confident.pooled fmt=pct--> reflects abstention, not
  accuracy: on its own, v2 would send every sealed pair to re-acquisition or a
  human. That is the job of the agent below.
- **Calibration is not good enough yet**: equal-count ECE is
  0.149 [SEALED]<!--src:results/sealed/v2_single.json#ece fmt=f3-->,
  and the pre-registered calibration rule failed.
- **The ambiguous tier is at the floor for every engine** (v2 top-1
  0.0% [SEALED]<!--src:results/sealed/v2_single.json#top1.ambiguous fmt=pct-->): when two replicas are
  indistinguishable in one frame, no single-shot matcher can break the tie.

### The agent on the sealed episodes

Virtual-SEM episodes seeded from the sealed seed: 48 [SEALED]<!--src:results/sealed/agent_rules.json#n_episodes fmt=int-->.
An episode is a success only if the arm commits a corrective stage move whose
drift estimate is within the grading tolerance of the true drift; an escalation
is never a success. Intervals are Wilson 95% CI. Both arms commit on the raw
rank-1/rank-2 margin threshold the agent uses, not on the calibrated threshold
of the pair evaluation above, which is why single-shot v2 commits here.

| Arm | Success | False commit | Escalation | Mean acquisitions | Mean dose (electrons) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Limitations

- All quantitative results use synthetic images from our virtual SEM; nothing
  has been validated on a real instrument or fab data.
- The evaluation ran on a development x86 machine, not on the COOL worker; the
  COOL campaign is reported separately in
  [docs/COOL_EVIDENCE.md](docs/COOL_EVIDENCE.md).
- v2 single-shot top-1 is below the v1 and NCC baselines.
- At the calibrated threshold v2 alone abstains on every sealed pair. The agent
  episodes commit on the agent's raw-margin threshold instead, so the agent's
  success is not a success rate over the sealed pairs.
- The agent's mean dose exceeds the pre-registered per-episode budget; the
  evaluation did not enforce the budget in the runner.
- The DRAM contour stage (S5) is a scaffold in this build.
- The pre-registered sealed gate did not pass; see the table above.

## Responsible use

See [docs/RESPONSIBLE_USE.md](docs/RESPONSIBLE_USE.md): synthetic data only,
human approval for every uncertain stage move, runner-enforced safety gates,
dose limits, seven-day retention, not validated on production tools.

`v1-munichtech`; it is the accuracy baseline above, not a contribution of this
